incoming_interface_paragraphs: The hypothesis $e>n$ in [[thm-separated-hecke-residues-give-seminormal-idempotents-and-bases]] cannot be dropped. Take $F=\mathbb C$, $q=-1$ (so $e=e(\mathbb C,-1)=2$, [[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]), $n=3$ and $\lambda=(2,1)$. The two distinct standard tableaux $s=\begin{smallmatrix}1&2\\3\end{smallmatrix}$ and $t=\begin{smallmatrix}1&3\\2\end{smallmatrix}$ have contents $\operatorname{content}_s(1),\operatorname{content}_s(2),\operatorname{content}_s(3)=0,1,-1$ and $\operatorname{content}_t(1),\operatorname{content}_t(2),\operatorname{content}_t(3)=0,-1,1$, and the extended quantum-integer identity gives $[1]_{-1}=1=[-1]_{-1}$, since $[-1]_{-1}=-(-1)^{-1}[1]_{-1}=1$. Hence $$([\operatorname{content}_s(k)]_q)_{k=1,2,3}=(0,1,1)=([\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q)_{k=1,2,3}\quad(q=-1):$$ the q-content sequences collide although $s\ne t$, so the separation conclusion of the theorem fails. The difference of the two putative separating eigenvalues at $k=2$ is $[-1]_{-1}-[1]_{-1}=0$. Thus interpolation cannot distinguish the two tableaux: a formula that excludes equal values may still define a polynomial, but it is not a separating projector for these two labels. The attempted generator formula has axial distance $\rho=2$ and $[\rho]_{-1}=0$. In fact $L_2$ has a nontrivial Jordan block on this cell, so this cell has no simultaneous JM-eigenbasis. This explicit example shows that the uniform separation hypothesis $e>n$ cannot be dropped; it does not claim that every individual cell at every parameter with $e\le n$ lacks a seminormal basis.

[F3] ([[thm-separated-hecke-residues-give-seminormal-idempotents-and-bases]]) Under the hypothesis $e>n$ the q-content sequence determines the standard tableau, and the denominators of the spectral projectors are nonzero.

$S^{\lambda}$ ([[def-type-a-hecke-specht-module-and-cell-form]],

$$d_{\mu\mu}=1\qquad\text{and}\qquad d_{\lambda\mu}\ne0\ \Longrightarrow\ \mu\unrhd\lambda,$$

([[def-dominance-order-on-partitions]]): a simple factor $D^{\mu}$ of
$S^{\lambda}$ can occur only if the $e$-regular label $\mu$ dominates
$\lambda$. Equivalently the decomposition matrix $(d_{\lambda\mu})$ is
unitriangular along dominance. This constrains but does not compute the
entries: no off-diagonal decomposition number is determined by cellularity.
